premises.text: People attend events to learn from content and to socialize, but online options only deliver learning
premises.evidence_span: People come to events for two reasons. To learn from great content and to socialize with people

premises.text: Teo puts customized avatars inside a shared virtual venue with hundreds of real people
premises.evidence_span: You appear inside of a venue. This is my avatar that I customized

premises.text: Users can move around and talk to people in the virtual venue as at a real event
premises.evidence_span: You can move around and actually talk to people, just like you're going to plan on doing today

premises.text: Distributed communities with no shared physical room can gather together on Teo
premises.evidence_span: They have two million entrepreneurs across 600 cities and no way to bring them together into the same room

premises.text: Revenue comes from monthly venue fees plus a share of ticket sales and virtual sponsorship
premises.evidence_span: charging organizations a monthly fee to have access to our venues

value.text: Virtual events that deliver both great content learning and real socialization
value.evidence_span: a product that gives the two benefits of why we are all here at this event online

secondary_value.text: Cross-border connections that could not be created otherwise
secondary_value.evidence_span: Creating connections that you could never create otherwise

causal_links.evidence_span: The world is missing a product that gives the two benefits of why we are all here at this event online
You can move around and actually talk to people
charging organizations a monthly fee to have access to our venues

notes: Livestream/webinar/AMA listed as one missing-socialization problem set. Avatar presence and talk treated as related product surface. Engagement duration coded as evidence not a premise. Singletons D1/D3/D4 retained as separately revisable modules.
